# Conversion

Turn each mirrored page into a Mintlify `.mdx` file. Preserve every heading, paragraph, list, table, code block and image. Do not summarize or reword.

Past about 50 pages, write a deterministic transformer script that reads the source (the repo, export or `mirror/`) and writes `.mdx`. When output is wrong, fix the rule and re-run the script; do not hand-patch generated files. Keep scripts outside the Mintlify project or list them in `.mintignore` (https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/mintignore.md).

Before writing the transformer, list every distinct custom tag, macro, directive, component, class and link scheme across the source and map each one. Unmapped constructs otherwise vanish or leak as raw text.

## Files

- Every page becomes an `.mdx` file.
- Mintlify never treats a file named `README.md` as a page, and serves `<dir>/index.mdx` at `/<dir>`. Rename a `README.md` that served its folder to `index.mdx`, and point links to `README.md` or `README` at the folder path.
- Partials and include targets are not pages; see Reusable content.

## Frontmatter

Every frontmatter field renders visibly: `title` is the page H1 and browser tab, `sidebarTitle` is the sidebar label, `description` is a subtitle under the H1, `icon` sits next to the sidebar entry. Copy from the source or omit. Never generate.

- `title`: the page's H1. Remove that H1 from the body so it does not render twice. If there is no H1, use the source's page title.
- `sidebarTitle`: only when the source nav label differs from the H1. If the nav label is longer than the H1, you extracted the wrong label (page `<title>`, breadcrumb, `og:title`); fix extraction.
- `description`: only when the source shows a subtitle or lead line directly under the title. Copy it verbatim, stripped of markdown and HTML. Never fall back to the first paragraph or a paraphrase of the title. No subtitle means no `description`. Many platforms use a frontmatter `description` only for meta tags, or derive one from the first paragraph; drop it unless the page showed it.
- `icon`: only when the source nav shows an icon for that page.
- Quote string values; if a value contains that quote character, use the other quote style. Never put JSX or HTML in frontmatter.
- Carry over other source frontmatter only when Mintlify has the same field with the same meaning; report the rest.

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/pages.md

## Components

Map source patterns to Mintlify components only when the meaning matches:

| Source                                     | Mintlify                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Note / info / tip / warning / danger boxes | `<Note>`, `<Info>`, `<Tip>`, `<Warning>`, `<Danger>`                     |
| Numbered procedures rendered as steps      | `<Steps>` / `<Step title="...">`                                         |
| Tabbed content                             | `<Tabs>` / `<Tab title="...">`                                           |
| Same snippet in several languages          | `<CodeGroup>`                                                            |
| Collapsible sections, FAQs                 | `<Accordion>` / `<AccordionGroup>`                                       |
| Link tiles, feature grids                  | `<Card>` inside `<CardGroup cols={2}>` or `<Columns>`                    |
| API parameter and response lists           | `<ParamField>` / `<ResponseField>`                                       |
| Inline definitions                         | `<Tooltip>`                                                              |
| Code blocks                                | fenced blocks with a language, plus `filename` when the source shows one |

Typed callouts (`<Note>`, `<Tip>`, `<Info>`, `<Warning>`, `<Danger>`, `<Check>`) take no `title` prop. Put a source callout title as a bold first line inside the callout; drop a title that only restates the type.

If the structure is ambiguous, leave it as plain markdown. A broken component is worse than a plain paragraph. Source components with no equivalent (interactive widgets, custom React or Vue, embeds) become a component snippet (Reusable content) or the closest static rendering of their content, and go in the report. Delete imports of the platform's component libraries once their usages are converted. Framework image and link components (`next/image`, `next/link`, `astro:assets` `<Image>`) become markdown images and links.

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/components/index.md

## Common source syntax

Several platforms share these. Source guides list their exceptions.

**Admonitions.** `:::type`, `!!! type` and similar blocks map by type:

| Type                                        | Mintlify    |
| ------------------------------------------- | ----------- |
| `note`, `example`                           | `<Note>`    |
| `info`, `important`, `abstract`, `question` | `<Info>`    |
| `tip`                                       | `<Tip>`     |
| `success`                                   | `<Check>`   |
| `warning`, `caution`                        | `<Warning>` |
| `danger`, `failure`, `bug`                  | `<Danger>`  |
| `quote`                                     | blockquote  |
| unknown                                     | `<Note>`    |

For `:::` containers, pair openers and closers before converting: a closing fence closes the nearest open container whose opening fence is no longer than it, so nested containers use a longer outer fence (`::::`). Text after the type on the opening line, or a `[Title]` label, is the title. An unclosed container runs to the end of its parent; a stray closer renders as text. If the old site already showed literal `:::`, report it rather than guessing the meaning.

**GitHub alerts.** `> [!NOTE]` → `<Note>`, `[!TIP]` → `<Tip>`, `[!IMPORTANT]` → `<Info>`, `[!WARNING]` → `<Warning>`, `[!CAUTION]` → `<Danger>`. Remove the marker line and the `> ` prefix from every line, including lazy-continuation lines. Text after the marker is the title. Convert them only where the platform rendered them as alerts; elsewhere they were plain quotes.

**Package-manager tabs.** Fences that the platform expanded into one tab per package manager (`npm2yarn`, ` ```npm ` and similar) become one `<CodeGroup>` with one fence per manager the live page showed, each titled with the manager name and holding the command as the live page translated it.

**Heading IDs.** Custom ids in any source syntax (`[#id]`, `{/* #id */}`, `{ #id }`, `:id=id`) become `## Heading {#id}`. Each platform slugifies headings differently from Mintlify: diff the old build's heading ids against `mint dev` and pin every anchor that content or inbound links target with `{#old-id}`.

**Code imports.** Directives that pull a source file into a fence (whole file, line range, region or anchor) become a fenced block holding exactly the selected lines, with the language, title and highlight meta carried over. Report each as a copy that will no longer track the file, or keep a prebuild script that regenerates it and say so. Fence options: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/create/code.md

**Template tags.** Never leave `{%` in MDX. Mintlify reads `{{name}}` as a `docs.json` `variables` entry (https://www.mintlify.com/docs/organize/settings-structure.md).

- Site-wide values: a `variables` entry used as `{{name}}`. Rename any name the schema rejects and record the mapping in the report. Take each value from the source config or a rendered page; never guess one.
- Page values (`page.x`, `$frontmatter.x`): inline the literal value.
- Logic (`if`, `for`, `assign`, `capture`, macro calls): replace with the output the production site showed; report each.
- `raw` wrappers: remove, keeping the content.

## Reusable content

Includes, partials and reusable blocks become snippets. An imported `.md` or `.mdx` file is a snippet, not a page, wherever it lives; files under `snippets/` always are, and any `.jsx` or `.tsx` file is a component snippet. Imports resolve against the importing file (`./x.mdx`, `../shared/x.mdx`) or the project root (`/shared/x.mdx`). Render with `import X from "./x.mdx"` and `<X />`; include parameters become props, read as `{param}` inside the snippet. Snippets never appear in navigation.

- **Source keeps its partials** (repo, or an export that ships them): each partial becomes exactly one snippet, imported wherever the source included it. Never paste copies. Keep the source's file layout and relative imports where they still resolve instead of moving everything into `/snippets/`.
- **Reuse already expanded** (most exports, live site): consolidate copies into one snippet only where they are identical.
- **Unused partials.** A partial nothing imports would publish as an orphan page. Do not copy it, or list it in `.mintignore`, and record it as `excluded` in the manifest.
- **Components.** Carry self-contained `.jsx`/`.tsx` components over as snippets, within the constraints at https://www.mintlify.com/docs/customize/react-components.md. Rename `.js` component files to `.jsx`: Mintlify loads every `.js` file as a site-wide script. One that imports an npm package other than `react` needs third-party libraries (https://www.mintlify.com/docs/customize/third-party-libraries.md); ask the user before relying on it. Components bound to the source framework (theme hooks, `next/*`, `@docusaurus/*`, Astro, Vue) map to Mintlify components or go in the report.
- **Single values** (product name, version) are `variables`, not snippets (Template tags above).

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/create/reusable-snippets.md

## MDX safety

MDX parses everything outside code fences as JSX. Normalize:

- `<https://example.com>` autolinks: use the bare URL.
- A bare `<` in prose (`<= v1.2`, `use < for less than`): `&lt;`.
- Placeholders like `<bucket-name>` in prose: wrap in backticks. Do not add backticks inside an existing inline code span.
- `{` and `}` in prose, tables and HTML cells: escape as `\{` `\}`.
- HTML: self-close void elements (`<br />`, `<img />`), use `className` not `class`, and `style={{ ... }}` objects, not strings.
- Component tags and fences go on their own lines with a blank line around them. `1. Do this. <Info>` becomes a list item, blank line, `<Info>`.
- Keep every component and fence balanced. Never emit a closing tag with no opener.
- Attribute values containing double quotes: use single quotes (`<Step title='Click "Save"'>`), not backslash escapes.
- Strip leftover wrapper `<div>`s from the source platform after converting their contents.

## Links

Rewrite internal links to root-absolute paths:

1. Find markdown links (not images) and `<a href>`.
2. Skip `http(s):`, `mailto:`, `tel:`, `#` and targets already starting with `/`.
3. Split off `#fragment` and `?query` and keep them.
4. Strip `.md`, `.mdx` and `.html`.
5. Resolve against the current file's directory. If the result escapes the repo root, leave the link alone and report it.
6. Prefix `/`.

Absolute links to the old docs domain become root-absolute paths too.

When the source links pages by id or title, build an id/title → path index from the whole inventory first, then rewrite links in a second pass. Links into content you did not migrate stay absolute and go in the report.

## Images and files

Download every image and linked file into the repo (for example `images/<page-path>/`) and point to it with a root-absolute path. Folders the platform served at the site root (`public/`, `static/`) are copied to the same paths at the Mintlify project root, so root-absolute URLs keep working without rewrites.

Exports and scraped pages often reference images by hosted URL without shipping the files. Collect every hosted asset URL from page bodies and embedded JSON blocks, download the original file (not a resized proxy), and rewrite the references. Keep alt text. If an image URL contains parentheses or spaces, use `<img src="/images/a (1).png" alt="..." />` instead of `![]()`, which breaks on them. macOS screenshot filenames put U+202F (narrow no-break space) before `AM`/`PM`, which the link checker does not match to a regular space: replace it with a space in both the filename and every reference (find them with `rg -l $'\u202f'`). Report any asset you could not download.

Wrap every standalone image (screenshots, diagrams, figures) in `<Frame>`. Sources never use this wrapper, so the transformer has to add it. A source caption goes in `caption`, verbatim; with no caption, use a bare `<Frame>`. Leave inline images unwrapped: icons, badges and logos inside a sentence, link, table cell or heading.

```mdx
<Frame caption="Caption from the source">
  ![Alt text from the source](/images/page-path/screenshot.png)
</Frame>
```

Reference: https://www.mintlify.com/docs/create/image-embeds.md, https://www.mintlify.com/docs/components/frames.md

## Port artifacts

Scraping composed widgets (cards, steps, tiles) to markdown leaves patterns that parse cleanly but render broken. Detect and fix them in the transformer before writing MDX.

- **A. Card link smash.** `[💬\n\n#### Title\n\nBody](/path)` becomes `<Card title="Title" icon="comments" href="/path">Body</Card>`.
- **B. Inline emoji card.** `[📋Sample apps](/path)` becomes `<Card title="Sample apps" icon="clipboard" href="/path" />`.
- **C. Link-wrapped steps.** `[1\n\n### Title\n\nBody](/path)` repeated becomes `<Steps>` with one `<Step title="Title">` each; the link goes at the end of the step body.
- **D. Orphan card.** An emoji line, a blank line, `#### Title`, then body, with no link around it. Consecutive triples become one `<CardGroup cols={2}>`. There are no brackets to search for, so test the detector on a known example.
- **E. `prism-code` fences.** Replace with the real language, detected from content (`import` python, `SELECT` sql, `{` json, `$ ` bash).
- **F. Admonition in frontmatter.** `description: ":::warning ..."` means the body admonition leaked. Remove the description (it was never a subtitle) and convert the body admonition.
- **G. Escaped placeholders.** `&lt;name&gt;` in prose renders literally; raw `<name>` breaks parsing. Both become `` `<name>` ``.
- **H. Stacked rules.** Consecutive `---` with nothing between them collapse into one or none.
- **I. Whole-page link.** An index page whose body is one giant `[...](...)`. Rebuild as a `<CardGroup>` with one card per entry. Find these by reading index and overview pages.
- **J. Chrome leakage.** "Copy page", "Edit on GitHub", "Was this helpful?", breadcrumbs, "On this page", prev/next footers. Strip during extraction.
- **K. Empty table header.** A header row of empty cells (`|  |  |`) renders as a blank strip. Rebuild real headers from the source, or drop the empty row so the first body row becomes the header.
- **L. Inlined generated data.** Machine-generated reference pages (field explorers, catalogs) scrape as huge inlined JSON. Write a dedicated converter that emits tables or `<ResponseField>` from that data.

Detector. Save it outside the docs folder, run `python3 detect.py mirror/` to plan transformer rules (ignore G on HTML mirrors), and `python3 detect.py .` on the converted repo until it prints nothing:

````python
import re, sys, pathlib
E = '[\U0001F000-\U0001FFFF☀-➿]'
P = {
  'A': rf'\[\s*{E}[^\]]*?####[^\]]*?\]\([^)]+\)',
  'B': rf'\[{E}+[A-Z][^\]]+\]\([^)]+\)',
  'C': r'\[\s*\d+\s*\n\s*\n\s*###[^\]]+\]\([^)]+\)',
  'D': rf'(?m)^{E}\s*\n\s*\n####\s',
  'E': r'```prism-code',
  'F': r'(?m)^description:\s*"?:::',
  'G': r'&lt;[A-Za-z0-9_-]+&gt;',
  'H': r'(?m)^---\s*\n\s*\n---\s*$',
  'J': r'(?m)^(Copy page|Edit on GitHub|Edit this page|Was this (page )?helpful)',
  'K': r'(?m)^\|(\s*\|)+\s*$',
}
for f in pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1]).rglob('*'):
    if f.is_file() and f.suffix in ('.md', '.mdx', '.json', '.html'):
        t = f.read_text(errors='ignore')
        hits = [k for k, p in P.items() if re.search(p, t, re.S)]
        if hits:
            print(f, ' '.join(hits))
````

## Icons

Mintlify icons default to Font Awesome (https://www.mintlify.com/docs/components/icons.md). Unknown names render as a blank slot, so never guess. Iconify names (`i-lucide-*`, `i-heroicons-*`, `i-simple-icons-*`) do not resolve: map each to an icon in the configured `icons.library` only on a clear match, otherwise drop it and report it.

Emoji used as icons:

| Emoji | Icon               | Emoji | Icon              |
| ----- | ------------------ | ----- | ----------------- |
| 💬    | `comments`         | 🔗    | `link`            |
| 🤖    | `robot`            | 🛡️    | `shield-halved`   |
| 🔍    | `magnifying-glass` | 🧠    | `brain`           |
| 📊    | `chart-column`     | ⚡    | `bolt`            |
| 🧪    | `flask`            | 🌐    | `globe`           |
| 📝    | `note-sticky`      | 🚀    | `rocket`          |
| 📄    | `file-lines`       | 🔌    | `plug`            |
| 📋    | `clipboard`        | 🔧    | `wrench`          |
| ⚙️    | `gear`             | ❓    | `circle-question` |
| 🤝    | `handshake`        |       |                   |

For anything else, pick the closest free icon from https://fontawesome.com/search?o=r&m=free.
